title: You Can't Prompt the Room: The Last Skill AI Won't Replace - Balázs Horváth, VisualLabs
talk_summary: A product/requirements talk arguing that since code generation is no longer the bottleneck, the scarce skill is eliciting what to build via user story maps, value/process/architecture thinking, and stakeholder access. It offers little on agent orchestration mechanics, but its concrete artifacts (user stories with acceptance criteria, a value/process/architecture doc in markdown) are directly usable as agent input specs.

takeaways.technique: User-story spec format as agent input
takeaways.what_they_do: Write every work item as persona + need + why plus acceptance criteria, then derive test cases from the criteria and chain stories into a spec before coding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every user story is actually made up with of these, you know, well-known structures, the persona, the what, the actual need, and the why

takeaways.what_they_do: Answer four questions (whose problem, what winning looks like, what blocks adoption, what decision it changes) and commit the answers as a markdown file the AI reads for context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just make sure that you track all of these in a good old markdown file in your repository so that AI can access it

takeaways.technique: Story-map MVP slicing to kill low-value work
takeaways.what_they_do: Map the user journey backbone, place stories beneath it, pick the first horizontal slice as MVP, and abandon ideas that create no business value.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 17 of those were abandoned because they actually created no um business value

takeaways.what_they_do: Replace 'features shipped' with 'features used more than twice' and track frequency of activity rather than time-on-site or demo success.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the number of features that we shipped that is actually used more than twice

takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately phrase specs in the well-known user-story structure because models were trained on it and pattern-match better.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you go back to something that's familiar to AI, it will get get you better better results
